Night-blooming cereus is the common name referring to many flowering ceroid cacti that bloom at night. The flowers are short lived, and some of these species, such as Selenicereus grandiflorus , each flower blooms for a single night, [ 1 ] though most put out multiple flowers over several weeks, each of which opens for only a single night.  Other names for one or more cacti with this habit are nightblooming frivolous , princess of the night , Honolulu queen (for Hylocereus undatus ), Christ in the manger , dama de noche , and queen of the night (which is also used for an unrelated plant species).
